question_stem:
A hot-air balloon floats just above the ground. The balloon is stationary and is held in place by a
vertical rope, as shown in Fig. 2.1.
The balloon has a weight W of 3.39 × 10^{4} N. The tension T in the rope is 4.00 × 10^{2} N.
Upthrust U acts on the balloon.
The density of the surrounding air is 1.23 kg m^{-3}.
question_stem_latex:
A hot-air balloon floats just above the ground. The balloon is stationary and is held in place by a
vertical rope, as shown in Fig. 2.1.
The balloon has a weight W of $3.39 \times 10^{4}\,\mathrm{N}$. The tension T in the rope is $4.00 \times 10^{2}\,\mathrm{N}$.
Upthrust U acts on the balloon.
The density of the surrounding air is 1.23 kg $m^{-3}$.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.question_text:
On Fig. 2.1, draw labelled arrows to show the directions of the three forces acting on the
balloon.
parts.question_text_latex:
On Fig. 2.1, draw labelled arrows to show the directions of the three forces acting on the
balloon.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.question_text:
Calculate the volume, to three significant figures, of the balloon.
volume = m^{3}
parts.question_text_latex:
Calculate the volume, to three significant figures, of the balloon.
$volume = m^{3} $

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.question_text:
The balloon is released from the rope.
Calculate the initial acceleration of the balloon.
parts.question_text_latex:
The balloon is released from the rope.
Calculate the initial acceleration of the balloon.

parts.label: (b)
parts.question_text:
The balloon is stationary at a height of 500 m above the ground. A tennis ball is released from
rest and falls vertically from the balloon.
A passenger in the balloon uses the equation v^{2} = u^{2} + 2as to calculate that the ball will be
travelling at a speed of approximately 100 m s^{-1} when it hits the ground.
Explain why the actual speed of the ball will be much lower than 100 m s^{-1} when it hits the
ground.
parts.question_text_latex:
The balloon is stationary at a height of 500 m above the ground. A tennis ball is released from
rest and falls vertically from the balloon.
A passenger in the balloon uses the equation $v^{2}$ = $u^{2}$ + 2as to calculate that the ball will be
travelling at a speed of approximately 100 m $s^{-1}$ when it hits the ground.
Explain why the actual speed of the ball will be much lower than 100 m $s^{-1}$ when it hits the
ground.

parts.label: (c)
parts.question_text:
Before the balloon is released, the rope holding the balloon has a strain of 2.4 × 10^{-5}.
The rope has an unstretched length of 2.5 m. The rope obeys Hooke’s law.
parts.question_text_latex:
Before the balloon is released, the rope holding the balloon has a strain of $2.4 \times 10^{-5}$.
The rope has an unstretched length of 2.5 m. The rope obeys Hooke’s law.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.question_text: Show that the extension of the rope is 6.0 × 10^{-5} m.
parts.question_text_latex: Show that the extension of the rope is $6.0 \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{m}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.question_text:
Calculate the elastic potential energy E_{P} of the rope.
E_{P} = J
parts.question_text_latex:
Calculate the elastic potential energy $E_{\mathrm{P}}$ of the rope.
$E_{\mathrm{P}}$ = J

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.question_text:
The rope holding the balloon is replaced with a new one of the same original length and
cross-sectional area. The tension is unchanged and the new rope also obeys Hooke’s
law.
The new rope is made from a material of a lower Young modulus.
State and explain the effect of the lower Young modulus on the elastic potential energy
of the rope.
